No band ends in a lighter or darker front-edge line followed by eave shadow, and no contents are visible. The board (rows 8-27, width 14) carries lettering and is a vertical face. The base at rows 28-30 is a thin dark strip. No receding side face is drawn. The result is a front elevation with no top surface, like the BAD front-elevation references.

styleAnswer.evidence: The candidate is a narrow vertical sign with a dark teal-green outline that visibly leans toward the panel colour. The measured near-neutral share of dark edge pixels is 0%, the same as all three references, so it is not a black sticker line. The body has about 4 steps: dark outline, mid panel, lighter edge highlight, and light text glyphs, with small detail dots on the lower part. That is slightly below the references' roughly 5 steps, but about level with bus-shelter-a. Measured density is 8 visible tones per tile with 0% near-flat coverage. That is above bus-shelter-a (6 tones, 9% flat) and below kiosk-a (12) and vending-a (20). Because the object is thin and sparse, it should be judged by eye, and a careful artist would accept it beside these references without it looking noticeably flatter. It has no large flat fills.
